sections.content: You know the conditional for advice from A2 Unit 26 and the *indefinido* from A2 Unit 11. New here is the *imperfecto de subjuntivo*, the form Spanish uses after *si* for an imagined situation: *Si yo fuera tú*, *si tuviera más tiempo*. The result goes in the conditional. To form it, take the *ellos* form of the *indefinido*, remove *-ron* and add *-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran*: *hablaron* gives *hablara*, *comieron* gives *comiera*, *tuvieron* gives *tuviera*.

sections.title: Imperfecto de subjuntivo: hablar, comer, vivir
rows: él, ella, usted hablara / comiera / viviera
he, she, you (formal) spoke / ate / lived
ellos, ellas, ustedes hablaran / comieran / vivieran
they, you all spoke / ate / lived

sections.title: Common irregular verbs (the same stem as the indefinido)

items.spanish: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con el profesor antes de cambiar de curso.
items.english: If I were you, I would speak to the teacher before changing courses.

items.spanish: Si tuviera más tiempo, leería el contrato otra vez.
items.english: If I had more time, I would read the contract again.
If you could choose, what would you do?

items.spanish: En tu lugar, buscaría una alternativa más segura.
items.english: In your position, I would look for a safer alternative.

sections.content: Never put the conditional after *si*: say *si tuviera*, not *si tendría*. *Si yo fuera tú* is the most common way to begin a piece of advice, and it is less direct than an imperative: the final decision belongs to the other person.
